question.problem:
Find $\text{E}[Y+1],$ given that random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡x,\, & 0\le x\le \frac{\pi }{2},\,0\le y\le \frac{\pi }{4}, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
Suppose $X$ and $Y$ are continuous random variables, and $f(x,y)$ is their joint probability density function. If $r:{R}^{2}\to R$ is a function of two variables, then the rule of the lazy statistician states that

$$
\text{E}[r(X,Y)]={∬}_{{R}^{2}}r(x,y)\,f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
r(x,y)=y+1.
$$

Notice that $f(x,y)$ is nonzero only in the rectangular region $D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le \frac{\pi }{2},\,0\le y\le \frac{\pi }{4}\}.$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y+1] & ={∬}_{{R}^{2}}(y+1)\,f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & ={∬}_{D}(y+1)\,f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}(y+1)\cdot \frac{4}{\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\frac{4}{\pi }(y+1){\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\frac{4}{\pi }(y+1)[\operatorname{sin}⁡x]_{0}^{\pi /2}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\frac{4}{\pi }(y+1)\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{4}{\pi }{[\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}+y]}_{0}^{\pi /4} \\  & =\frac{4}{\pi }(\frac{{\pi }^{2}}{32}+\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =\frac{\pi }{8}+1.\end{aligned}
$$
